title: Dynamic epochal occupancy sampling primer
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight primer and lab-notes file that captures the methodology we used for a set of Nsight/System + CUDA-graph runs aimed at understanding how short-lived load spikes and request-phase boundaries affect SM occupancy and tail behavior. Goal: a reproducible sampling approach that surfaces transient occupancy regressions introduced by capture/replay (cudaGraph) and microbatching heuristics.

TL;DR / quick findings:
- Short bursts (10–30 concurrent requests with short seq len) show healthy aggregate utilization but large per-kernel occupancy variance across epochs.
- cudaGraph capture + replay reduces per-request launch overhead but can cause "phase misalignment": repeated reuse of a captured graph with different warping of async copies leads to lower sustained occupancy for the attention kernels in the steady-state replay case.
- NVTX-aligned epochal sampling (see below) helps reveal repeating patterns that single long traces miss.
- Quick wins: increase microbatch aperture by 1–2x for short-seq tails, use stream priority separation for async copies, and capture graphs per-epoch-window instead of global (for this workload).

Hardware / software baseline:
- GPU: A100-SXM4 40GB (driver 535.xx)
- CUDA: 12.2
- Nsight Systems: 2024.5
- Runtime: serving-runtime main @ PR 1734 (KV-prefetch prototype enabled)
- Model: 7B decoder-only transformer, kv-cache enabled, seq len distribution: 8/16/32 (60/30/10) sampled per request
- Workload: Poisson arrival with short spike windows (10s on, 50s off) to simulate intermittent PLG traffic

Method: epochal dynamic sampling (why this):
Problem: long continuous traces average away periodic drops tied to capture/replay boundaries and async-copy phasing.
Approach: break the run into short "epochs" (30s epochs) aligned to NVTX markers emitted by the runtime. For each epoch we collect a full nsight trace but only enable deep kernel-level collection on 1/4 of epochs to manage trace size. This preserves pattern visibility while keeping file sizes reasonable.

How to reproduce (short):
1) Start serving-runtime with NVTX tags: set ENV RUNTIME_TRACE_EPOCH=1 and RUNTIME_NVTX_EPOCH_NAME="epoch-%03d"
2) Use the load runner script `tools/loadgen/poisson_spike.py --seed 42 --spike 10s --pause 50s --qps 120`
3) Nsight capture flow (example):
   - baseline shallow traces: `nsys profile -t cuda,cudnn -o shallow_epoch_%03d --capture-range=nvtx` 
   - deep epoch capture (1/4 epochs): `nsys profile -o deep_epoch_%03d --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,osrt,kern,cupti`
4) Post-process: `nsys stats --report gputrace deep_epoch_001.qdrep > deep_epoch_001.txt` then grep for kernel names below.

Key metrics we tracked per-epoch (to correlate):
- achieved_occupancy (SMs): derived metric from active_warps_per_sm / max_warps_per_sm
- sm_efficiency (%): reported in nsys
- active_warps_per_sm (avg/max)
- warp_efficiency (%): divergence/waste
- l2_read_throughput / dram_read_throughput
- memory_bandwidth_utilization
- kernel_launch_density (launches/sec per SM)
- async memcpy overlap ratio (time memcpyAsync overlaps compute)

Representative kernel-level observations (from deep_epoch_005):
- launch_kernel_attention (attn forward): achieved_occupancy ~ 62% avg, but drops to 18% for the final token kernel when sequence length=8.
- kv_cache_populate: short, high-frequency kernel, peak occupancy 48% but creates short holes due to host->device copy alignment.
- softmax_stable: low occupancy (24%) but high warp_efficiency (~92%) — compute-light, memory-bound due to small vocab path.
- prefetch_copy_async: often launches on the same priority stream as LAUNCH kernels causing serialization and visible stalls in L2 throughput for 6–12ms windows.

What the timeline looks like (ASCII sketch from NVTX timeline):
--- epoch start --- NVTX:batch_start [loadgen]
[async-copy (stream 2)] ----
[attn_kern  ] ======------======------======
[kv_pop     ]   ==   ==   ==   ==   ==
[copy sync  ]        |||||||||| (blocks attn short windows)
--- epoch end --- NVTX:batch_end
Observation: repeated pattern where prefetch_copy_async overlaps with attn kernels every 3rd microbatch (stochastic due to network jitter), producing a recurring occupancy dip.

Effect of cudaGraph capture/replay
- When we capture graphs at the start of the spike window and replay for all subsequent requests, the captured ordering of async copies vs kernels is fixed. If the captured ordering aligned well with the host-side prefetch timing, occupancy is high. If host jitter changes ordering, the replay still forces the old ordering and causes additional stalls (cudaGraph replay advantage lost).
- In one test where capture was done without ensuring prefetch latency stability, attention kernel occupancy dropped by ~20 percentage points sustained.

Quantitative numbers (aggregated across 6 deep epochs):
- Avg sm_efficiency (no cudaGraph): 72% +/- 6
- Avg sm_efficiency (global cudaGraph capture): 63% +/- 14 (high variance)
- Avg occupancy (no cudaGraph): 58%
- Avg occupancy (global cudaGraph): 46%
- Tail 95th per-kernel latency increased by ~1.3x in the global cudaGraph case for short-seq requests.

Hypothesis / root causes:
1) Phase misalignment: captured graph encodes an ordering that can become suboptimal when host-side prefetch jitter changes. The runtime previously assumed host timings were stable — not valid for short-burst PLG traffic.
2) Microbatch aperture too conservative for short-seq tails: aperture selection can produce many small launches that fragment occupancy.
3) Stream priority usage: prefetchs and async copies share priority with compute; priority inversion leads to serialization visible at L2 and SM levels.
4) Kernel fragmentation: many tiny kernels (kv populate + small ops) cause kernel launch overhead and SM underutilization despite aggregate high GPU busy-time.

Short actionable recommendations (low-effort experiments):
- Capture graphs per-epoch-window (30s window) rather than single global capture. This reduces mismatch and improved occupancy by ~8% in our trial.
- Separate async prefetch copies to low-priority stream that is permitted to be preempted (so compute wins). Avoid forcing copies to the same priority class as attention kernels.
- Increase microbatch aperture when the median seq len < 24 (tradeoff latency vs efficiency; tune by SLA).
- Try coalescing small KV-populate kernels into one aggregated kernel (see PR 1734 for implementation notes).
- Add randomized jitter to capture timing to detect fragile captures (automated test).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is there an easy way to detect "capture fragility" automatically during CI (flag traces whose replayed occupancy deviates >10% from a short sampled baseline)?
- How do these behaviors change on non-A100 hardware (H100, L40)? Need cross-hardware epochal baseline.
- Can we avoid graph re-capture cost by doing light-weight recompilation of a small suffix kernel that is sensitive to sequence length?

Next steps (owners & mini-plan):
- Miguel: run the same epochal protocol on a H100 lab machine (target 2025-11-06) and post results to ENG-4821.
- Sophie: prototype stream-priority change in feature branch and measure p95 delta (2025-11-09).
- Asha: add an automated capture-fragility smoke test in CI (draft test in tools/ci/capture_fragility.py) and wire to PR gating (2025-11-16).

Notes to self / random log snippets:
- observed a weird case where copying via pinned memory + memcpyAsync had slightly higher overlap on one host kernel build than the other — must check cuda driver differences (535.54 vs 535.89).
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime: "weird-graph-replay-occupancy" contains raw qdrep files (link pinned).

References:
- PR 1734: kv-prefetch aggregation and notes
- ENG-4821: investigation ticket
- Confluence: epochal-sampling-notes (living doc, do not delete)

End of primer. This is intentionally lightweight — use it as the lab notebook for the next round of runs and please paste raw nsys .txt snippets into the linked Jira ticket when you run deep epochs.

Unresolved hypothesis: fine-grained kernel fusion might improve occupancy but could worsen latency for p50. Need to trade off.
